judgments.reasoning_cat1: A five-limb trigger followed by three cumulative conditions; 'any Claim arising out of or in any way involving any transaction or event' is very broad, and limb (1) captures the creation of any non-bank entity however small.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is replaced wholesale by the Mergers endorsement (c179), which changes the threshold from 25% to 20%, and is then deleted entirely by the Discovery Period Activation (c006), so which version governs depends on layering three documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single automatic-coverage rule keyed to an objective asset percentage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is superseded by the 20% version in the Mergers endorsement (c180) and is the cross-reference on which the Section IV(E) definition of 'Company' depends, yet Section XII was later deleted in its entirety.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bar on prior Wrongful Acts is expressed with the sweeping 'directly or indirectly resulting from' and reaches back to any 'fact, circumstance or situation' before the transaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion V(O) excepts claims 'as provided in Section XII (C)(3)', but this subsection has only limbs (1) and (2), and the Mergers endorsement leaves it unchanged while the Discovery Period Activation deletes the whole section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence says the Insurer returns only 90% of unearned premium, then the multi-year sentence limits 90% to cancellations before the first anniversary and gives pro rata afterwards, so the two rules overlap awkwardly for this three-year policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XIII(C)(2) says the Policy 'may not be cancelled and the entire premium shall be deemed fully earned' once a conversion event occurs, which contradicts the Named Insured's unqualified right to cancel here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Notice periods and mechanics are stated in precise days and by certified mail; little play in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This subsection is deleted and replaced by the Iowa Amendatory Endorsement (c187), which substitutes a closed list of permissible cancellation reasons, so the original text is no longer operative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Ceasing to engage actively in its primary business' is a vague trigger for cutting off coverage, and 'conversion' is used without definition for a run-off effect.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limb (2) preserves the right to buy the Discovery Period after 'any of the foregoing events', but Section III grants that right only on conversion 'subject to Section XIII (C)(1)(b)' — a direct inconsistency about eligibility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Relative legal exposures of the parties' is an inherently indeterminate allocation standard, and limb (1)(a)'s 100% rule for joint Loss sits oddly beside limb (2)'s proportional rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section XIV(B) supplies an arbitration route for Defense Costs allocation only, leaving allocation of other Loss without a mechanism, which is a gap rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Insurer, if requested by the Insured, shall submit the allocation dispute to binding arbitration' makes arbitration available only at the Insured's election, and the clause is confined to Defense Costs — a mandatory/permissive asymmetry of the kind courts construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is limited to Defense Costs while Section XIV(A)(2) allocates all Loss, and Section XVI(F) separately conditions any action against the Insurer, so the dispute-resolution architecture is uneven.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) says the Application is construed as a separate application by each Insured Person while limb (2) says the Policy is not a series of individual contracts, two statements that pull in opposite directions on severability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That tension is compounded by Section XV(B) and (C), which sever knowledge for some Insureds but impute senior officers' knowledge to the Company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing sentence — the conditions apply 'whether or not the Insured Person actually knew if the misrepresentation ... was made' — contradicts limb (1), which voids coverage only for an Insured Person 'who knew' of the undisclosed fact.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also has to be squared with Section XV(A)(1)'s separate-application construction and with Section XV(C)'s severability of exclusions, which take a different approach to imputed knowledge.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The imputation rule is precise as to whose knowledge counts and to which exclusions it applies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It imputes knowledge only for Section V exclusions (G) and (H), leaving the Section VI and endorsement exclusions unaddressed, and it cuts across Section XV(A)(2)'s statement that the Policy is not a series of individual contracts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conventional subrogation and cooperation language with no ambiguous operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Insured vs. Insured exclusion and the Other Insurance clause without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The entire-agreement sentence and the assignment sentence are run together with a comma splice, but each is intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It names 'this Policy, the Application, and any written Endorsements' as the whole agreement, which differs slightly from the Declarations' formulation (c018) and the Section IV definition of 'Policy'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conformity clause that amends unspecified terms to match unspecified laws; broad, but the mechanism is standard and self-executing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Iowa Amendatory Endorsement performs the same function specifically for cancellation, so the general clause and the specific one overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For all purposes under this Policy including, but not limited to' followed by specifics is an open catch-all about the scope of one insured's authority to bind the others.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It concentrates authority in the 'Named Insured', a role that shifted when Vantus Bank was added at the head of Item 1 (c025), and it sits against Section XV's severability of each Insured Person's position.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear anti-waiver and written-endorsement-only rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement mechanism used throughout and with Section XVI(B).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all the terms of this Policy' as a condition precedent is a sweeping requirement, and the final determination clause has a stray 'a)'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the arbitration provision in Section XIV(B) and the several other condition-precedent clauses (Sections X, XI), which together make the route to recovery cumulative.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making all Loss excess to 'any other existing insurance regardless of whether collectable' is broad, and the carve-out for policies written as specific excess of this one creates a potential circularity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section II(B) already makes not-for-profit directorship coverage excess, and Section XVI(J)'s anti-stacking rule addresses overlapping Progressive policies differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete ten-day production obligation tied to a defined term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the cancellation and nonrenewal provisions without friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite statement that insolvency neither releases the Insurer nor deprives it of rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in direct tension with the Insolvency Exclusion (c083), which excludes any Claim 'in any way involving' the Financial Impairment of the Company, and with the Conversion provision's cut-off on Financial Impairment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rule is stated twice over ('shall not ... exceed the largest available Limit of Liability' and 'creates a sublimit'), which is clumsy but not genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Securities Liability endorsement (c175) deletes and replaces this very subsection and adds a further anti-overlap sentence, so the operative stacking rule is the endorsement's.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional headings clause, plainly worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several endorsements identify the provisions they delete purely by their headings ('Section II (B), entitled "Not-for-Profit Directorships"'), which sits uneasily with the statement that headings form no part of the terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line amending preamble.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement mechanism in Section XVI(E).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Arising out of or in any way involving the purchase or sale of, or offer to purchase or sell, any securities issued by the Company' is very wide, and the saving sentence points to a form number rather than to a defined Insuring Agreement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Declarations Item 6 states that Broad Form Company Liability 'includes coverage for ... Securities Liability', which this exclusion removes from every agreement except Form 5098, so the two documents point different ways.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the policy inception date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings language limited by 'other than as above stated'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant runs to 'the Insured' generally rather than to Insured Persons or the Company separately, which blurs which retention and which limit apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That undifferentiated grant has to be fitted to Section VII(B)'s retention scheme and Section VIII's order of payments, both of which are built around Insuring Agreements (A), (B) and (C).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scoping sentence introducing exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the hinge for reading the endorsement against the base Policy, but says so expressly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion identified by section number and title.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same deletion is made by two other endorsements, which is duplicative but consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear: all Section V exclusions apply except the Brokerage/Advisory Services Exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It leaves the Section V exclusions applying to this endorsement while Section VI's exclusions (expressed to apply only under Insuring Agreement (C)) are separately re-imported below, which is workable but requires cross-reading.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad 'directly or indirectly ... or for the benefit of' language, but the claimant class is identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the identical Section VI(A) exclusion, adding nothing inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A compact fee-dispute exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the Company's services' inside a Brokerage/Advisory endorsement whose grant runs to 'the Insured', a slight mismatch, and it overlaps the Loss definition's carve-out (7).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The counterfactual proviso 'unless such liability would be imposed regardless of the existence of such contract' is hard to apply in practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Loss definition's contractual carve-out, which uses different words and its own Defense Costs reimbursement rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (1) excludes claims 'in any way involving' the Financial Impairment of the Company — i.e. its own receivership — while the proviso restores cover only for investments in the stock of limb (2)/(3) entities, a lopsided rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As with Section VI(D), this pulls against Section XVI(I)'s statement that Financial Impairment does not release the Insurer, and the proviso conspicuously omits limb (1).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific categories with a modest 'provider of like services' tail; the missing colon after 'providing' is cosmetic.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Section VI(E) without variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (6), 'any other investment banking activity', is a general catch-all after five specifics, raising the usual ejusdem generis question inside a brokerage coverage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against the Brokerage/Advisory Services definition, which affirmatively covers investment advisory and financial planning work, so the boundary between the grant and this exclusion needs reconciling.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual or written representations, promises or guarantees' is very probably a mis-transcription of 'oral or written', and as it stands 'actual' representations is close to meaningless — a mechanical error that changes the exclusion's reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Brokerage/Advisory grant but does not contradict any other provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete exclusion for machine failure; 'any machine or system of machines' is broad but plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses mechanical failure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Whether 'the Company's function or activity as receiver' reaches claims brought by a receiver appointed over the Company is arguable on the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Section VI(I) and interacts with the Financial Impairment definition and Section XVI(I) in the same contested way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-statute exclusion; 'arising out or in any way involving' drops a word but the sense is unmistakable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare effective date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard savings language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate consideration recital.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No tension found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant covers Wrongful Acts 'resulting from the Administration of any Employee Benefit Plan' or violation of ERISA duties, resting on two defined terms whose fit ('Administration' is a narrow clerical definition) is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The base policy's Wrongful Act definition is confined to acts in the capacity of director, officer or IRA/Keogh trustee, which does not obviously reach plan-fiduciary conduct that this endorsement covers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scoping sentence introducing exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly signals the cross-reading required.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line deletion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicated in two other endorsements, consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Counseling Employees with respect to, interpreting, handling records in connection with, or effecting enrollment or cancellation' is a narrow clerical list that may not cover investment or funding decisions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insuring Agreement and the replaced Insured vs. Insured exception both turn on 'Administration', so the narrowness of this definition constrains coverage the endorsement appears to grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Operated solely by the Company or jointly by the Company and a labor organization' is a restrictive formula, and 'operated' is not the ERISA term of art.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The replaced Insured definition (c152) extends to plans 'acquired during the Policy Period pursuant to Section XII', a section the Discovery Period Activation deletes, leaving the class of insured plans uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'By its express terms or as a result of surrounding circumstances' imports an open factual inquiry into what should be a definitional line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It nests inside the Employee Benefit Plan definition and is used consistently in the endorsement.
